solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Waffle is effective in council factory?

blocks.note: to gas is to talk idly, to waffle
something that is effective works

explanation.surface: Someone complains that empty talk passes for action at a local council meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: gasworks were often run by town councils.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasworks is a plant producing town gas, historically owned and operated by municipal authorities, hence a factory of the council.

clue.text: Section of raga, this

indicators.note: a section is a piece cut from something longer, so the answer is a run of letters inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A musician points to one passage in an Indian melody.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the answer is a section of a raga and also a section of the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Gath is the second movement of a raga in Indian classical music, where rhythm enters.

clue.text: Signs of thrush in a path he retraced

indicators.note: retraced suggests going over the course again in a different way, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spots a thrush on a path he walks again.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrush is the songbird in the surface but the fungal infection in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphthae are small white ulcers in the mouth, the characteristic marks of oral thrush infection.

clue.text: Mouthpieces disturbed pope less inserting jab

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown out of order, so these letters are mixed up
inserting means putting one thing inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a poke is a jab

explanation.surface: Church spokesmen are upset that the pontiff gets a dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouthpiece is someone who speaks on behalf of others, exactly what spokespeople do.

clue.text: Full ramble by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word is identified by how it is spoken, not how it is written

blocks.note: a ramble is a walk

explanation.surface: A long country walk is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full' looks like an adjective (a full ramble) but is the cloth-making verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Wauk is a Scots verb meaning to full cloth, thickening it by beating and moistening.

clue.text: A dividing shaft in mine-passage

indicators.note: something dividing a word sits in its middle, splitting it in two

blocks.note: a rod is a shaft
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dividing shaft is described within a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaft' and 'mine' paint one picture, but the shaft is just a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: In mining, a road is an underground passage or gallery along which miners and coal travel.

clue.text: Country with irises etc gleaned wild in South Dakota

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so these letters run loose into a new order
in places the jumbled letters inside the state abbreviation

blocks.note: SD is the abbreviation for South Dakota
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wild irises are gathered in the plains of South Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' means a stretch of land, as in open country, not a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedgeland is low-lying ground covered with sedges, rushes and irises, a kind of open country.

clue.text: Seats arranged back to front in marshy spot

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken from the back and placed at the front

blocks.note: pews are church seats

explanation.surface: Someone sets out chairs facing the wrong way at a soggy site.
explanation.definitionFit: Spew is a dialect word in Chambers for a wet, boggy patch of ground where water oozes out.

clue.text: Lassie's to make trial of grip as I wrestled with late pregnancy condition

indicators.note: things wrestled are twisted about, so these letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: pree is Scots for to taste or try, so a Scottish lassie's word
a clamp is a grip
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl tests her grip while wrestling, late in pregnancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lassie' signals a Scots word; Lassie is not the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-eclampsia is a dangerous condition of high blood pressure arising in the later stages of pregnancy.

clue.text: First of brood prevailed with no outsiders

indicators.note: having no outsiders means the letters at either end are dropped

blocks.note: to reign is to prevail, as in 'silence reigned'

explanation.surface: The firstborn of a family won out, with strangers kept away.
explanation.definitionFit: Eigne is a legal term meaning eldest or firstborn, from Old French for the elder child.

clue.text: Refuse container maybe doubles up in dray (8, two words)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
in places the turned word inside the vehicle

blocks.note: a wain is a farm wagon, like a dray
doubles are bets on two races

explanation.surface: A refuse lorry's bins fold double on the cart.
explanation.walkthrough: A double is a bet on two selections, the winnings from the first riding on the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A waste bin is a receptacle for rubbish, one example of a refuse container, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Dismay to cut from contract

indicators.note: cutting one thing from another removes it, so the short word is taken out of the longer one

blocks.note: taken as written
an appalto is a contract or monopoly, from Italian

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified to be dropped from a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like the infinitive marker joining definition and wordplay, but it is the very pair of letters removed from APPALTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or horrify someone, which is a stronger way of saying dismay as a verb.

clue.text: Evergreen shrub in a role I distributed round area

indicators.note: things distributed are spread about, so these letters are scattered into a new order
round says the rearranged letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A gardener's part is handed out around a planted area.
explanation.definitionFit: Olearia is the genus of daisy bushes from Australasia, evergreen shrubs with daisy-like flowers.

clue.text: One of the Chilognatha like this round Ohio dangles oddly

indicators.note: round says the first word wraps around the abbreviation that follows
done oddly means done in a strange way, so these letters are put in a strange order

blocks.note: thus means in this way, like this
O is the US postal-style abbreviation for Ohio
taken as written

explanation.surface: A zoologist describes a millipede wriggling its many limbs strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chilognatha are the main order of millipedes, and thousand-legs is an old name for a millipede.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousandlegs is a popular name for a millipede, a creature belonging to the zoological order Chilognatha.

clue.text: Very old woman on board sled's awfully bold

indicators.note: someone on board is inside the vehicle, so she sits within the other letters
done awfully means done badly, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the possessive read as plain letters
aunt is an obsolete word for an old woman or gossip

explanation.surface: An elderly woman sledging is remarkably brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very old' marks the obsolete sense of aunt, an old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dauntless means fearless and not easily discouraged, so bold in spirit.

clue.text: Too much booze, not good, as part of hop

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for good is dropped

blocks.note: a binge is a bout of heavy drinking
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Overdrinking is bad, beer's hops included.
explanation.walkthrough: The hop is the plant, not a jump; it ties the surface to beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bine is the flexible climbing stem of the hop plant, so one component of it.

clue.text: Former grasp, in that case with shifting of time

indicators.note: the letter standing for time is moved from its place to the other end

blocks.note: then means in that case, as in 'then do it'

explanation.surface: An old hold is described as shifting over time.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the usual abbreviation for time; it moves from the front of THEN to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Hent is an obsolete verb meaning to seize or take hold of, so 'former' marks the archaic use.

clue.text: Knight to applaud governor installed

indicators.note: something installed is put in place inside, so the official goes within the applause

blocks.note: to cheer someone is to applaud them
a vali is a governor of a Turkish province

explanation.surface: A knight is applauded as a governor takes office.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevalier is a knight or member of an order of chivalry such as the Legion of Honour.

clue.text: Part of heat-resistant layer in saloon at speed?

definitions.note: the answer names the whole tile covering, with 'part of' loosely marking it as one component of a spacecraft's shielding

blocks.note: a saloon is a type of car
apace means quickly

explanation.surface: A fast saloon car is fitted with a heat shield.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is a British car with a separate boot, a sedan.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers defines carapace as the heat-resistant tiles covering a spacecraft, borrowing the word for a crab's hard shell.

clue.text: Noisy bird from Australia caught by rifle?

indicators.note: a thing caught by another is held inside it

blocks.note: a rifle is an example of a gun, hence the question mark
A is a standard abbreviation for Australia

explanation.surface: A loud bird from Australia is shot by a hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: The guan is a large, noisy tropical American bird related to the curassow, known for loud calls.

clue.text: Thick and bushy part of leaf, rosy

indicators.note: a part is a piece taken out of something longer, so the letters sit within the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the comma

explanation.surface: A rosy leaf is thick and bushy.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro hairstyle is a thick, rounded, bushy mass of tightly curled hair, so the word serves as an adjective.

clue.text: E.g. spoon set

blocks.note: first meaning: a spoon is an old wooden golf ...
second meaning: a group or society of people

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests laying cutlery; a spoon is also an old name for a lofted golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Club names a golfer's implement, of which the spoon was one, and also a set or association of people.

clue.text: On the way home, mounted on trotting nag, look in

indicators.note: a trotting horse moves its legs in a jumbled rhythm, so these letters are shuffled about
in puts the short exclamation inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: a rider who is mounted is up
taken as written
lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: A rider heads home on a trotting horse and calls in on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Upalong is a West Country dialect word meaning homewards, or on the way home.

clue.text: Traveller with ordinary recovery of property

blocks.note: a rep is a commercial traveller, a sales representative
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: A salesman arrives with a regular repossession job.
explanation.definitionFit: Repo is short for repossession, the seizing back of goods or property when payments are not kept up.

clue.text: Achievement indicated by poetry by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the sense comes from the sound of the spoken word, not its spelling

blocks.note: poetry is measured in metrical feet

explanation.surface: An accomplishment is apparently marked by verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Poetry stands for its units of rhythm, the metrical feet, rather than for any poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A feat is a notable deed or accomplishment, especially one requiring skill or courage.

clue.text: Mature love in Paris, about the first thereof

indicators.note: the first of the city just named means its opening letter only
about means surrounding, so the French word goes round the letter

blocks.note: rien is French for nothing, and love means nothing in tennis
the opening letter of the city

explanation.surface: A grown-up love affair in Paris is described.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis, so in French it becomes the word for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to mature or become fully developed, as fruit does.

clue.text: Circus star, no good with arms not waving around

indicators.note: waving things move to and fro, so these letters are shifted into a new order
around says the jumbled letters enclose the short abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A circus performer flops because his arms stay still instead of waving.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongman is a performer who displays feats of strength, a traditional circus attraction.

clue.text: Power attached to charged particle, source of nuclear force

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
an ion is an electrically charged atom or particle

explanation.surface: A physicist describes power linked to a charged particle at the heart of the nucleus.
explanation.definitionFit: The pion, or pi meson, is exchanged between nucleons and accounts for the strong force binding atomic nuclei.

clue.text: Local flat, more than 50% financial support raised

indicators.note: more than half means only the majority of letters is kept and the rest dropped
in a down clue, raised means read upwards

blocks.note: welfare is state financial support

explanation.surface: A local flat gets most of its funding raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' marks a dialect word, not a pub or neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Flew is a dialect word meaning flat or shallow, so a local form of flat as an adjective.

clue.text: Druggie turning up to begin again? Not me

indicators.note: not me means the letters of that pronoun are dropped
in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to resume is to begin again
taken as written

explanation.surface: An addict shows up again wanting to restart, but insists it is not them.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who takes illegal drugs habitually, so a druggie in slang.

clue.text: See duck escape through hedge, giving us the slip

indicators.note: giving someone the slip means escaping them, so the named pair of letters goes
completes the idiom of escaping from someone, which drops the letters for the pronoun

blocks.note: a smeuse is a gap in a hedge used by an animal to escape
taken as written

explanation.surface: A duck darts through a hedge and gives its watchers the slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Smee is a dialect name for the smew and similar ducks such as the pintail and widgeon.

clue.text: Orchard's beauty, boor's deprivation a Brit admits

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the Brit takes the other pieces inside

blocks.note: taken as written
pom is Australian slang for a Briton
a pleb is a coarse, common person
deprivation is loss

explanation.surface: A British visitor concedes that a lout has been robbed of the orchard's loveliest sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boor's deprivation' is read as two words run together, the boor and his loss, rather than as a possessive; pom is Australian slang for a Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple blossom is the pink and white flowering of apple trees, the spring glory of any orchard.

clue.text: The church is installing form of steel piano pedal

indicators.note: installing something means putting it inside, so the church abbreviation goes around it
a form of something is a version of it reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church is fitting a steel component to its piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeste is a soft pedal on a piano that muffles the tone by interposing felt between hammers and strings.

clue.text: Late-flowering rot excised in net

indicators.note: excised means cut out, so these letters are removed from the longer word

blocks.note: serotine means flowering or appearing late in the season
taken as written

explanation.surface: Decay is cut out of a late-blooming plant caught in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rot' looks like part of the gardening picture, but it is the three letters removed from SEROTINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A seine is a large fishing net that hangs vertically with floats above and weights below.

clue.text: Sink to invigorate runs away

indicators.note: something that runs away leaves, so that letter goes from the word

blocks.note: to renew is to restore vigour
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A tonic is poured down the sink and the runs disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: Enew is a Spenserian falconry word meaning to plunge or drive a bird into water, so to make it sink.

clue.text: Draining jug held by pundit

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed within it

blocks.note: a sage is a wise, learned person
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: An expert pours out a jug and holds it empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewerage is the system of draining waste water and sewage away through sewers, so drainage as a noun.
